SELECT c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.concept_class_id, c.vocabulary_id, COUNT(DISTINCT de.person_id) AS n_patients, COUNT(*) AS n_exposures
FROM omop.drug_exposure de

WHERE LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%methylphenidate%'
   OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%amphetamine%'
   OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%dextroamphetamine%'
   OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%lisdexamfetamine%'
   OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%atomoxetine%'
   OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%guanfacine%'
   OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%clonidine%'

GROUP BY c.concept_id, c.concept_name, c.concept_class_id, c.vocabulary_id

I have the exposure data. Now let me group these into the neurotransmitter pathways they align with and aggregate. The ADHD drug mechanisms cluster into three pathways:

- **Dopamine/norepinephrine releasers & reuptake inhibitors (stimulants)**: methylphenidate, dexmethylphenidate, amphetamine/dextroamphetamine salts, lisdexamfetamine
- **Selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors**: atomoxetine (and viloxazine)
- **Alpha-2 adrenergic agonists (noradrenergic)**: guanfacine, clonidine

One caveat in the raw pull: clonidine is heavily used for non-ADHD indications (hypertension, sedation, injection/epidural forms), and apraclonidine is an ophthalmic drug — not ADHD-relevant. Let me aggregate cleanly, excluding apraclonidine, so the pathway comparison reflects the actual ADHD-relevant agents.

arguments.sql_query:
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%methylphenidate%'
      OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%amphetamine%'
      OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%dextroamphetamine%'
      OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%lisdexamfetamine%'
      THEN 'Dopamine/NE stimulant (releaser/reuptake inhibitor)'
    WHEN LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%atomoxetine%'
      OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%viloxazine%'
      THEN 'Selective NE reuptake inhibitor'
    WHEN LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%guanfacine%'
      OR (LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%clonidine%' AND LOWER(c.concept_name) NOT LIKE '%apraclonidine%')
      THEN 'Alpha-2 adrenergic agonist (noradrenergic)'
  END AS pathway,
  COUNT(DISTINCT de.person_id) AS n_patients,
  COUNT(*) AS n_exposures
FROM omop.drug_exposure de
JOIN omop.concept c ON de.drug_concept_id = c.concept_id
WHERE (LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%methylphenidate%'
   OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%amphetamine%'
   OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%dextroamphetamine%'
   OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%lisdexamfetamine%'
   OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%atomoxetine%'
   OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%viloxazine%'
   OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%guanfacine%'
   OR (LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%clonidine%' AND LOWER(c.concept_name) NOT LIKE '%apraclonidine%'))
GROUP BY
  CASE
    WHEN LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%methylphenidate%'
      OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%amphetamine%'
      OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%dextroamphetamine%'
      OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%lisdexamfetamine%'
      THEN 'Dopamine/NE stimulant (releaser/reuptake inhibitor)'
    WHEN LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%atomoxetine%'
      OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%viloxazine%'
      THEN 'Selective NE reuptake inhibitor'
    WHEN LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%guanfacine%'
      OR (LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%clonidine%' AND LOWER(c.concept_name) NOT LIKE '%apraclonidine%')
      THEN 'Alpha-2 adrenergic agonist (noradrenergic)'
  END
ORDER BY n_exposures DESC;

| **Alpha-2 adrenergic agonist** (noradrenergic) | clonidine, guanfacine | 32,472 | **534,334** |
| **Dopamine/NE stimulant** (releaser + reuptake inhibitor) | methylphenidate, amphetamine/dextroamphetamine salts, lisdexamfetamine, dexmethylphenidate | 28,427 | **283,405** |

**Most frequently used pathway: the alpha-2 adrenergic (noradrenergic) agonists** — clonidine + guanfacine — with ~534K exposure records, roughly double the dopamine/norepinephrine stimulant class.

Single most-prescribed agents:
- **Clonidine 0.1 mg tablet** — 15,206 patients / 275,122 exposures (the single largest contributor)
- **Methylphenidate 5 mg tablet** — 5,626 / 42,717 (top stimulant)
- **Guanfacine 1 mg tablet** — 3,334 / 30,439

### Important caveat
The alpha-2 count is inflated by **clonidine used outside ADHD** — it's widely prescribed for hypertension, sedation/withdrawal, and pain (note the many injectable/transdermal/0.2–0.3 mg forms in the raw data). If you restrict to agents that are predominantly ADHD-specific, the **dopamine/NE stimulants are the most-used ADHD pathway**, with guanfacine as the leading noradrenergic ADHD agent.
